html:
The Omani Empire was the sea empire that Oman built after driving out the Portuguese, stretching at its height from the Gulf to Zanzibar and the coast of East Africa, and to Gwadar in today's Pakistan.

The Ya'ruba imams and then the Al Bu Said dynasty, which took power in 1744, ruled it from Muscat. Omani fleets took Mombasa in 1698, and Omani governors and merchants settled along the Swahili coast. The empire lived on trade in ivory, cloves and enslaved Africans.

Its greatest ruler, Said bin Sultan, moved his court to Zanzibar. After his death in 1856 his sons split the realm, and the Sultanate of Zanzibar became separate from Muscat. The Omani Arab elite ruled Zanzibar until the revolution of 1964.
sum: The Omani Empire was the sea empire that Oman built after driving out the Portuguese, stretching at its height from the Gulf to Zanzibar and the coast of East Africa, and to Gwadar in today's Pakistan.
